name: FreeHosting.com
tagline: Free web hosting with 10GB storage and no forced ads on your site
description: FreeHosting.com offers lifetime-free web hosting with 10GB storage, unlimited bandwidth and no forced ads, plus a $7.99/mo paid tier for multi-site needs.
about: FreeHosting.com is a no-cost web hosting service aimed at hobby sites, students and anyone testing a small project before committing to paid hosting. The free plan includes 10GB of disk space, unmetered bandwidth (subject to a fair-use policy), one MySQL database, one email account, PHP/MySQL support and a control panel for managing files, domains and email from one dashboard. Unlike many free hosts, it doesn't inject third-party ads into hosted sites, and there's no trial countdown — the free plan is meant to run for as long as the domain is active.

The free tier is single-site only and requires bringing your own registered domain; it does not provide a free subdomain to get started. It also lacks SSH access and cron job scheduling, both of which are reserved for the paid plan. For anyone outgrowing the basics, FreeHosting.com sells a paid tier at $7.99/month with 100GB storage, multi-site hosting, and unlimited email accounts and databases.

Independent reviews on Trustpilot paint a rough picture of the actual experience: a 1.8-out-of-5 rating from 41 reviews, with recurring complaints about being pushed to buy a $29.95 SSL certificate to make the free site usable, slow or unanswered support tickets, and sites getting intermittently rate-limited or taken offline. Treat the free plan as a genuinely limited sandbox rather than a reliable home for anything that matters.
policies: FreeHosting.com's free plan has no stated trial period or expiration as long as the underlying domain stays registered and active, but reviewers report the account can be suspended or rate-limited without much warning. Paid plans are billed as ordinary subscriptions; check FreeHosting.com's own terms and billing page for its current refund and cancellation policy before entering payment details, since multiple Trustpilot reviewers report billing disputes.
